messages.subject: chapter 5, pp. 67-68
parts:
Dear all,

I'm replicating the book ggplot2, and I couldn't replicate the code below.

Can someone help me?

df <- data.frame(
  x = c(3, 1, 5),
  y = c(2, 4, 6),
  label = c("a","b","c")
)
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y, label = label)) +
  xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL)
p + geom_point() + opts(title = "geom_point") # ???
p + geom_bar(stat="identity") +
  opts(title = "geom_bar(stat=\"identity\")") # ???
p + geom_line() + opts(title = "geom_line") # ???
p + geom_area() + opts(title = "geom_area") # ???
p + geom_path() + opts(title = "geom_path") # ???
p + geom_text() + opts(title = "geom_text") # ???
p + geom_tile() + opts(title = "geom_tile") # ???
p + geom_polygon() + opts(title = "geom_polygon") # ???

Best,
--
Gabriel Cepaluni

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: chapter 5, pp. 67-68
parts:
I mentioned this a few weeks ago on the ggplot2-dev list. The problem
is that you have label as an aesthetic in the original ggplot() call
and ggplot2 expects to see it in every subsequent layer. One
workaround is to add group = 1 as an aesthetic:

p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y, label = label, group = 1)) + xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL)

Now rerun the plot calls again and they should work. I just checked
several of them in the upcoming version 0.9.0 and they all worked fine
with the above change. It should be the same in 0.8.9. [Aside: There
will be a few other places where the book code breaks when the new
version is released, so be prepared.]

Taking label out of the aes() statement in ggplot() would also work:

p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) + xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL)

The only line of code you would need to change would be the one
involving the label in geom_text():

p + geom_text(aes(label = label)) + opts(title = "geom_text")

This would be the preferred way of doing things because the variables
mapped in ggplot() through aes() are expected to be present in every
subsequent layer of the plot. You can always add aesthetics in a
geom_*() call, and in fact it's done rather often, even in the book.

HTH,
Dennis
